statement: Build a singly linked list from the given values and print how many nodes it contains. Count by walking the chain from the head until the next pointer runs out - the count must come from the walk, since a list in the wild does not carry its length with it.
constraints: When n is 0 the second input line is empty.

example.why: The walker makes five visits before hitting the end of the chain.

hint: Initialise the counter at zero so the empty chain answers itself.
mistake: Starting the counter at one to account for the head - an empty list then reports a ghost node.
